title: Insurance Claim Services: Several Claim Files for One Customer
content:
**Policy.** A customer may hold any number of claim files at once, one for each carrier claim; landlords, property managers and associations often have several losses open across their properties, and one insured can have claims with different carriers. Each claim file stands on its own: deductibles, approvals and carrier payments are never moved between claim files.

This is the Insurance Claim Services rule on how many claim files one customer may hold. No limit per customer is set.

## What the rule means on the records

| Question | Answer under the policy |
|---|---|
| How many claim files may one customer hold? | Any number, one for each carrier claim. |
| May one insured have claims with different carriers? | Yes. |
| May a deductible assessed on one file be applied on another file? | No; deductibles are never moved between claim files. |
| May a carrier approval or carrier payment recorded on one file be used on another? | No; approvals and carrier payments stay on the file they were recorded on. |

*Example (hypothetical):* a property manager holds two claim files with two different carriers for losses at two buildings. A carrier payment received on the first file stays on the first file, even when the second file still has an approved amount unpaid.
